concept.name: Rolling mean
concept.definition: The rolling mean is the arithmetic average of a series over a trailing window of fixed length that slides forward one observation at a time. Applied to prices it is the simple moving average (SMA), the most common trend-smoothing statistic in market analysis.
concept.intuition: The rolling mean smooths out bar-to-bar noise by averaging the last N values, so the line rises when recent values are generally higher than the ones dropping out.
concept.mechanics: For window length w, sum the last w observations and divide by w at each step. pandas rolling(window).mean() labels the result at the right edge of the window and returns NaN for the first w−1 points by default (min_periods=w for fixed windows).
concept.formula: μ_t = (1/w) Σ_{i=0}^{w−1} x_{t−i}, where w is the window length.
concept.failure_modes: The mean lags the series by roughly half the window and is distorted by outliers, since each extreme pulls the average for w periods. Equal weighting of the oldest and newest observations is arbitrary; window changes can flip signals.
concept.misconceptions: A moving-average crossover is a descriptive smoothing artifact, not a proven predictive signal; and the SMA is not 'the fair price' — it is a trailing average.
concept.example: A 5-day rolling mean of closes 100, 102, 101, 103, 104 is (100+102+101+103+104)/5 = 102.0 on the fifth day.
